text: You are likely referring to the LLM Wiki (often phrased as "LLM Wiki"), a popular framework popularized by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy. It refers to a method of using Large Language Models to automatically organize raw notes and documents into a structured, interlinked wiki. It is designed to solve the problem of forgetting information by acting as a persistent "memory layer" rather than a chat session that resets. The 3-Layer Structure An LLM Wiki operates on three distinct layers: 1. Raw Sources: Your original, unedited documents (PDFs, articles, notes, transcripts). The AI reads these but never modifies them. 2. The Wiki: A folder of AI-generated, interlinked markdown files that represent the compiled knowledge (concepts, entities, summaries). The LLM owns this layer and updates it when new sources are added. 3. The Schema: A configuration document (often called CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md ) that tells the AI exactly how to structure the wiki, handle new sources, and maintain formatting. How it compares to traditional RAG Traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): The AI searches raw documents every single time you ask a query. It only works with what you feed it at that moment. LLM Wiki: The AI compiles and synthesizes the knowledge once into a living knowledge base. You add a new document, the LLM extracts the key information, and integrates it seamlessly into the existing network of pages.
